serverInfo.name: replenishradar
serverInfo.title: ReplenishRadar MCP Server
serverInfo.description: Inventory forecasting and replenishment for Shopify and Amazon sellers: stock levels, stockout forecasts, reorder suggestions, sales analytics and suppliers over MCP. Create purchase orders and send them only after human approval.

schemes.description: API key with rr_sk_ prefix. Generate keys in Settings > API Keys at app.replenishradar.com. Organization is derived from the key -- no separate header needed.
Sign-in connector for Claude and ChatGPT: a ReplenishRadar admin or owner signs in on a consent page and chooses what the assistant may do. No API key. Add this address as a custom connector.

sandbox.description: No-signup, read-only sandbox keys let you try the real read tools against synthetic demo data before signing up. Responses are tagged {"sandbox": true}.
sandbox.acquisition: Cold start, no auth, no POST required: GET https://api.replenishradar.com/api/public/agent-intake?tier=B&channels=shopify,amazon&sku_count_band=500_2k&store_count=2&primary_pain=stockouts&autonomy_intent=read - a positive verdict returns a short-lived read-only sandbox key plus a stand-up kit. The same endpoint accepts a POST with a JSON body if you have one. If you cannot hold a key at all, the read tools are also runnable with no key at https://api.replenishradar.com/api/public/demo. The rr_evaluate_fit MCP tool returns the same verdict but requires a key, so use it to re-qualify in-session, not as the first step.
sandbox.expires: short-lived (hours); rotate by requesting a new one

transport.note: Native MCP over HTTP JSON-RPC (initialize / tools/list / tools/call) at /api/mcp. Initialization and tool discovery are public metadata; tool calls require an rr_sk_ bearer token. A custom REST shape ({"tool":...,"input":...}) is also available at /api/mcp/call and is what the npx @replenishradar/mcp-server stdio bridge uses.

discovery.human_demo_store_note: The real dashboard on a synthetic catalog, no signup and no login. There IS a public interactive demo; hand this link to the seller you are answering for.

requirements.tier: Standard includes read and basic_write API/MCP access; Growth adds sensitive_read and sensitive_write; Scale and Enterprise increase limits.
requirements.writeAccess: Write tools require a write-scope API key plus the required capability and selected tool group.
requirements.rateLimiting: Per-key hourly limits with circuit breaker protection

docs.title: MCP Server Documentation
docs.description: Connect your AI agent to live Shopify and Amazon inventory data via the Model Context Protocol.

accessTiers.write: Basic-write tools only when selected on the key

tools.name: rr_get_suggested_purchase_orders
tools.description: Get AI-suggested purchase orders based on stockout risk, demand, and supplier reliability.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_list_purchase_orders
tools.description: List purchase orders with status, amounts, and delivery info. supplier_delivery_status is the supplier email outcome: pending (being sent), emailed, partial (some recipients only), queued (will send after the recipient's quiet hours), unknown (could not confirm, check with the supplier before resending), failed, or null (never emailed).

status.description: Filter: draft, sent, received, cancelled (comma-separated for multiple)

search.description: Part of a PO number to match.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

offset.description: Deprecated: rows to skip. Use cursor; it stays correct while rows change.

tools.name: rr_get_purchase_order
tools.description: Get detailed info for a specific purchase order. supplier_delivery_status says whether the supplier got the PO email: pending, emailed, partial, queued, unknown (could not confirm, check with the supplier before resending), failed, or null (never emailed). The lines come in pages, oldest first in a stable order: pass next_cursor as cursor until has_more is false; the purchase order's own fields are on every page. Landed costs are allocated over all lines, so each line's landed_cost_per_unit is the whole order's figure; the cost scope that says whether those costs can be relied on is cost_scope on the purchase order, not on each line.

po_id.description: The purchase order id or its PO number, for example REV-PO-002

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_po_pdf
tools.description: Find where to open a purchase order as a PDF. Returns the PO number and the address in ReplenishRadar that renders the PDF, not the file itself.

po_id.description: The purchase order id or its PO number, for example REV-PO-002.

tools.name: rr_get_po_documents
tools.description: List the documents attached to a purchase order, newest first.

po_id.description: The purchase order id or its PO number, for example REV-PO-002

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_po_notes
tools.description: Get all notes for a purchase order, most recent first.

po_id.description: The purchase order id or its PO number, for example REV-PO-002

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_replenishment_actions
tools.description: List canonical replenishment actions for buyer work. Prefer this over suggested purchase orders or alerts when deciding what action the user should take next.

kind.description: Optional kind filter: supplier_po, transfer, combined, no_action

destination_location_id.description: Optional parent or child destination location filter

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_replenishment_action
tools.description: Get one replenishment action with child item provenance, snapshots, linked execution records, and event history. The products come in pages: pass next_cursor as cursor until has_more is false; the action's own fields are on every page. The action carries its newest events, oldest first, up to 100 (fewer when they are long); events_total is how many it has and events_truncated is true when older ones were left out, which are on the action's page in the app. Long lists of SKUs or locations on the action are capped at 100 with a <name>_total beside them; the product pages are the complete list.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_transfer_exclusions
tools.description: Why products were, or were not, moved between the seller's own locations on the last transfer run. Pass a sku for one product's answer; omit it for the whole population with counts by reason. Use this when a seller asks why something was not transferred or restocked from another location, rather than inferring it from an empty transfer-suggestions list.

sku.description: One product's answer. Omit for the population. There is deliberately no store filter: the transfer census is org-grain, because transfer generation resolves its locations org-wide.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_stockout_risk
tools.description: Get stockout risk assessment for SKUs. Returns risk levels, days to stockout, velocity, and planned_order: the quantity the PO planner suggests ordering (use planned_order.qty, not suggested_qty). A row with planned_order null and a name_review_hold has an order waiting on the supplier name review, which is not the same as no order suggested. Only positions the planner could evaluate are listed: products without enough sales history and products excluded from planning are left out, so absence from this list, or an empty list, is not evidence that stock is healthy.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_inventory_position
tools.description: Get current inventory positions (on-hand, in-transit, sellable) for a SKU. sellable_qty is what each location can sell now (Amazon FBA: on_hand, Amazon's fulfillable units). available_qty is the channel's own figure, null where the channel reports none (Amazon); null means not reported, not zero. SKU is required.

sku.description: SKU to look up. Give this or item_id.

item_id.description: The product's item id. Give this or sku.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_demand_forecast
tools.description: Get demand forecast for a SKU including predicted demand, seasonal factors, and the item's forecast track record: whether its forecast has historically beaten a naive same-as-last-week baseline, or whether there is too little scored history to judge. seasonal_profile on the first page gives the 12-month seasonal curve behind the forecast's seasonal_index, which level supplied it (item, family, supplier or store), how it is graded, and the coverage window with the dates the index averages over. SKU is required.

sku.description: SKU to forecast. Give this or item_id.

item_id.description: The product's item id. Give this or sku.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_list_items
tools.description: List inventory items with optional filters. For an exact SKU identity question, provide the exact value in search and set include_listing_identity=true to resolve Amazon seller SKUs and return source listing identifiers such as ASIN and FNSKU.

include_listing_identity.description: Set true only with an exact search value for a SKU identity question. Resolves an exact Amazon seller SKU even when it differs from the canonical SKU and returns listing source, ASIN, and FNSKU evidence.

needs_review.description: true: only items flagged for review; false: only items not flagged.

vendor_id.description: Only items whose primary supplier is this supplier id (from rr_list_suppliers).

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

offset.description: Deprecated: rows to skip. Use cursor; it stays correct while rows change.

tools.name: rr_list_suppliers
tools.description: List suppliers with performance metrics.

include_skus.description: Also list each supplier's SKUs. Default false.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_sales_history
tools.description: Get sales history rows, newest first, over a time period. total is the exact number of rows in the window; count is the rows in this page. When has_more is true, pass next_cursor as cursor to get the next page. Answer totals and rankings from total or rr_get_top_sellers rather than from the rows, and do not conclude anything about the whole window from a partial walk.

granularity.description: day (default) returns daily rows for up to 90 days. month returns one row per calendar month for up to 36 months, for one SKU or, with no SKU, the store's totals.

months.description: Months of history when granularity is month (default 12, max 36). Net demand units; the newest month may be partial.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_top_sellers
tools.description: Get top-selling products ranked by units sold over the whole window, one row per product however many SKU labels its sales carry. total_skus is how many products have sales rows in the window (the name is historical); truncated_to_top_n is true when that is more than the page returned (this ranking has no next page).

months.description: Rank over this many calendar months instead of days (max 36), on net demand units. Use for a window longer than 90 days.

tools.name: rr_get_slow_movers
tools.description: Overstock / dead-stock / slow movers: SKUs you are HOLDING (on-hand > 0) that aren't selling - capital tied up. Returns on_hand, units sold in the window, and a dead_stock flag: held with no sale in the last 12 months, whatever the window (null, with dead_stock_message saying why, while the sales history is too short to decide). dead_stock_summary is the seller's total dead-stock count across every store, whatever store_id asks for, and its value at cost when costs may be shown. Inventory-first, so never-sold dead stock is surfaced too. total is how many held SKUs there are; has_more is true when that is more than the page returned.

limit.description: Number of slow movers per page (default 20, max 500).

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_inventory_value
tools.description: Get total inventory value (units and value across all active locations).

store_id.description: Only stock at this store's locations.

tools.name: rr_get_sku_health
tools.description: Org-wide SKU health snapshot: stockout-risk counts by level and active alert counts by type.

tools.name: rr_get_lost_sales
tools.description: Get estimated lost sales due to stockouts.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_sync_status
tools.description: Get sync status for connected stores. Pass the sync_event_id returned by rr_trigger_sync to get that request's own receipt (sync_event) and its attempts (sync_event_attempts) alongside recent runs.

sync_event_id.description: Optional sync-event UUID from rr_trigger_sync. Adds that request's receipt and attempt history to the response.

connector_type.description: Optional filter for the recent-runs list.

store_id.description: Optional store UUID filter for the recent-runs list.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_store_health
tools.description: Diagnose each connected store's health. Returns per-store connection status, hours since last sync, and a diagnosis enum (disconnected / error / pending_setup / sync_paused / stale / healthy), plus a summary with primary_diagnosis. Call FIRST for any sync-failure, missing-inventory, or 'why isn't X working' question - a disconnected store is upstream of every sync error it has.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: rr_get_data_freshness
tools.description: Get per-dimension freshness status (sync, positions, demand, risk, recommendations) with staleness thresholds and a primary_concern summary. Use it when the user asks whether the numbers are up to date, or to explain a figure that looks stale.

tools.name: rr_get_setup_status
tools.description: Check onboarding milestones and compute the next setup step. Returns counts (connected_stores, suppliers, items), activation milestones, and a next_step enum (connect_store, wait_for_sync, add_supplier, run_first_forecast, review_first_suggested_po, done). Call for onboarding questions or before suggesting reorder points / deeper features - don't advise a number when next_step is still connect_store.

tools.name: rr_get_recent_activity
tools.description: Summarize the last N days of org activity (default 7, max 30). Returns counts only - alerts created/resolved, POs created/received, sync runs total/failed, and a one-word headline (sync_health_degraded / alert_storm / receiving_active / normal / quiet_week). No monetary fields. Use for 'what should I focus on today?' or 'what happened this week?' - one call replaces a fan-out of five.

tools.name: rr_get_alerts
tools.description: Get active alerts (stockout warnings, sync failures, anomalies).

sku.description: Only alerts for this product, under any SKU it has had.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

offset.description: Deprecated: rows to skip. Use cursor; it stays correct while rows change.

tools.name: rr_get_agent_context
tools.description: Read one saved agent context entry by namespace and key. Expired entries are not returned. The namespace must have been granted to this API key by an admin.

namespace.description: A context namespace this key has been granted, for example supplier_rules.

key.description: The entry's key within the namespace, up to 200 characters.

tools.name: rr_list_agent_context
tools.description: List the entries stored under an agent context namespace, most recently updated first.

key_prefix.description: Only keys starting with this prefix

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Pass it with the same other inputs until has_more is false.

tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.description: Search the ReplenishRadar knowledge base for product features, best practices, and inventory management concepts. Use for questions that aren't answered by the seller's live data.

top_k.description: Number of results to return (default 5, max 10)

tools.name: rr_evaluate_fit
tools.description: Check whether ReplenishRadar fits a seller from a few facts about their business, and get a fit verdict. Reads no store data and needs none. Answers can be sent as fields or nested under answers; pass the returned attribution_token on a follow-up call to continue.

sku_count_band.description: Roughly how many products they stock.

primary_pain.description: The inventory problem they most want solved.

autonomy_intent.description: How much the agent will do: read only, prepare drafts, or act.

answers.description: The same answers as one object, instead of the fields above. Any other question from the public agent-intake survey may be included.

tier.description: Which question set these answers complete. Default A.

attribution_token.description: The token a previous call returned, to continue the same evaluation.

tools.name: rr_submit_feedback
tools.description: Send feedback to the ReplenishRadar team on the user's behalf. Call it only after the user has said yes to your question "Want me to pass this to the product team?" in this conversation. Describe what the user wanted and what happened, in your own words, with no names, contact details, credentials, or store data beyond what the report needs. After it returns success, tell the user what you sent. Sending the same message twice returns the first report and files no second one.

type.description: bug: something is broken or wrong. suggestion: something the user wishes ReplenishRadar did. support: the user needs help. other: anything else.

message.description: What the user was trying to do, what happened, and what they expected.

impact.description: Optional: how much this is holding the user back.

related_tool.description: Optional: the ReplenishRadar tool the feedback is about, by name.

tools.name: rr_create_purchase_order
tools.description: Create a draft purchase order for a vendor. Status is ALWAYS 'draft' - agents cannot create approved/sent POs directly. Use rr_request_approval to request approval; the PO must be approved before it can be sent. Returns the new PO + items_added count.

destination_location_id.description: The id of the location the goods will arrive at.

items.description: Required line items: [{sku, quantity, unit_cost}, ...]. The server validates quantities, constraints, and trusted cost fallbacks.

quantity.description: Quantity to order for this SKU.

unit_cost.description: Optional unit cost; the server falls back to a trusted cost when omitted.

notes.description: Optional free-text notes to attach to the draft PO.

expected_delivery_date.description: Optional expected delivery date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

action_id.description: Optional replenishment action UUID to link to the draft PO.

tools.name: rr_import_purchase_orders
tools.description: Import open and historical purchase orders from a CSV export (the way in for a seller moving from another inventory tool). One row per line item, grouped by po_number; column names from common inventory tools' exports are recognized automatically. Records received quantities as a snapshot only - it NEVER moves stock. Idempotent on po_number (re-running the same file is safe). preview defaults to true: it validates and returns what would import without writing; pass preview=false to actually import. Returns per-PO counts, warnings, and errors.

csv_content.description: Raw CSV text. Required columns: po_number, vendor_name, sku, quantity. One row per line item; up to 500 POs / 5000 lines.

preview.description: Default true. When true, validates and returns what would import without writing. Pass false to commit the import.

create_missing_vendors.description: Default false. When true, suppliers not yet in the org are created as name-only stubs instead of erroring those POs.

default_location_id.description: Destination location UUID for PO rows without a warehouse column, when the org has more than one warehouse.

import_cancelled.description: Default false. When true, cancelled/void POs in the file are imported under their cancelled status instead of being skipped.

default_lead_time_days.description: Optional. Lead time in days (0-3650) pre-filled on any supplier stub this import creates, so the imported catalog isn't left with missing-lead-time gaps. Omit to set lead times later.

tools.name: rr_update_purchase_order
tools.description: Update a draft or suggested PO. Allowed fields: notes, expected_delivery_date, vendor_id. Edits are recorded in the PO's revision history. Status changes are NOT supported here - use rr_send_purchase_order or rr_cancel_purchase_order. Only draft/suggested POs are editable; approved/sent/received/cancelled POs are not.

po_id.description: The purchase order id or its PO number, for example REV-PO-002 (required).

notes.description: Optional replacement notes for the PO.

expected_delivery_date.description: Optional expected delivery date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

vendor_id.description: Optional vendor UUID to reassign the PO to.

tools.name: rr_add_po_note
tools.description: Add a note to a purchase order. Use for context the seller wants to attach to the PO record (e.g., 'vendor confirmed lead time').

po_id.description: The purchase order id or its PO number, for example REV-PO-002 (required).

tools.name: rr_request_approval
tools.description: Ask a manager to approve a draft/review PO. The request expires in 15 minutes and is approved in ReplenishRadar after signing in, not by a link. Use BEFORE rr_send_purchase_order - sending without approval will fail. Supersedes any prior pending request.

po_id.description: The purchase order id or its PO number, for example REV-PO-002 (required).

tools.name: rr_send_purchase_order
tools.description: Send an approved PO: marks it sent (status='sent', sent_at=now) and emails the supplier the PO packet at the supplier's contact on file. Will fail if status is not 'approved' - use rr_request_approval first. The response's delivery and supplier_delivery_status say what happened to the email, one of six values: pending (being sent), emailed, partial (some recipients only), queued (will send after the recipient's quiet hours), unknown (could not confirm, check with the supplier before resending) or failed. Calling it again on a sent PO sends nothing. To email an already-sent PO's supplier again, pass resend: true: a failed email, or the recipients a partial one missed, are sent again; when the supplier may already have it (emailed or unknown) nothing is sent unless confirm_possible_duplicate is also true, so check with the user first; while queued or pending a resend is refused.

po_id.description: The purchase order id or its PO number, for example REV-PO-002 (required).

action_id.description: Optional replenishment action UUID to record the send event on.

resend.description: Email the supplier again for a PO already sent (sent, confirmed, pi_received or in_transit). Does not send the PO again.

confirm_possible_duplicate.description: With resend: true, send even though the supplier may already have this order (delivery emailed, partial or unknown). Only after the user has confirmed it.

tools.name: rr_cancel_purchase_order
tools.description: Cancel a PO (status='cancelled'). Cannot cancel POs already in cancelled/received/closed status.

po_id.description: The purchase order id or its PO number, for example REV-PO-002 (required).

tools.name: rr_record_pi_review
tools.description: Record a supplier's proforma invoice (PI) on a purchase order: its number, date, total and payment terms. A sent or confirmed order moves to pi_received; one already at pi_received has its PI details updated; any other status is refused. Send only the fields the seller gave you.

po_id.description: The purchase order id or its PO number, for example REV-PO-002.

pi_date.description: The invoice date, ISO 8601, for example 2026-10-18.

pi_terms.description: The payment terms as a JSON object under 4 KB, for example {"deposit_pct": 30, "balance": "on shipment"}.

tools.name: rr_add_replenishment_action_note
tools.description: Add a note to a canonical replenishment action. Use this when the seller wants context attached to the action itself, not just a PO.

tools.name: rr_dismiss_replenishment_action
tools.description: Dismiss a canonical replenishment action when the seller decides no buyer work is needed. Records an action event and removes it from active action queues.

tools.name: rr_prepare_replenishment_action
tools.description: Preview a replenishment action before acting on it: its kind, status, products, supplier and locations, and its current updated_at. Pass that updated_at as expected_updated_at to rr_execute_replenishment_action, rr_retry_replenishment_action or rr_resolve_replenishment_action. Changes nothing; refused for an action that is already finished.

action_id.description: The replenishment action id, from rr_get_replenishment_actions.

tools.name: rr_execute_replenishment_action
tools.description: Turn a replenishment action into its draft purchase order or draft transfer, for a person to review. Nothing is sent to a supplier and no stock moves. It needs the action's updated_at as last read; if the user has not given it, read it with rr_prepare_replenishment_action.

action_id.description: The replenishment action id, from rr_get_replenishment_actions.

idempotency_key.description: A value you choose for this attempt. Repeating a call with the same value and the same arguments returns the first result and does nothing again.

expected_updated_at.description: The action's updated_at as last read (rr_prepare_replenishment_action or rr_get_replenishment_action). The call is refused if the action changed since, so it can be read again.

tools.name: rr_resolve_replenishment_action
tools.description: Close a replenishment action with a reason when no purchase order or transfer is needed, for example because the stock was bought another way. Removes it from the open lists and creates nothing.

action_id.description: The replenishment action id, from rr_get_replenishment_actions.

reason.description: Why no purchase order or transfer is needed.

idempotency_key.description: A value you choose for this attempt. Repeating a call with the same value and the same arguments returns the first result and does nothing again.

expected_updated_at.description: The action's updated_at as last read (rr_prepare_replenishment_action or rr_get_replenishment_action). The call is refused if the action changed since, so it can be read again.

tools.name: rr_retry_replenishment_action
tools.description: Try again to turn a replenishment action into its draft purchase order or draft transfer after an earlier attempt was blocked or failed. Same effects as rr_execute_replenishment_action: drafts only, nothing sent and no stock moved.

action_id.description: The replenishment action id, from rr_get_replenishment_actions.

idempotency_key.description: A value you choose for this attempt. Repeating a call with the same value and the same arguments returns the first result and does nothing again.

expected_updated_at.description: The action's updated_at as last read (rr_prepare_replenishment_action or rr_get_replenishment_action). The call is refused if the action changed since, so it can be read again.

tools.name: rr_create_location
tools.description: Create a manual stocking location: a warehouse, 3PL, FBA, WFS, in-transit or inbound location, with an optional address. Refused when an active location already has the name. It adds the location only; set its stock with rr_set_stock_at_location.

name.description: The location's name, unique among active locations.

is_default.description: Make this the default manual location. Default false.

tools.name: rr_set_stock_at_location
tools.description: Set the on-hand quantity of one SKU at one manual location to an absolute number, replacing the stored count. Read the current position first and confirm the number with the user: a sale recorded since the last count is overwritten. System and inactive locations are refused, and so is stock a live collection holds.

location_id.description: The manual location's id. Give this or location_name.

location_name.description: The manual location's name, used when location_id is not given.

quantity.description: The new on-hand quantity, 0 or more.

tools.name: rr_acknowledge_alert
tools.description: Acknowledge an open alert. Sets status='acknowledged', stamps acknowledged_at + acknowledged_by, and writes an alert_audit row. Use when the seller has read and accepted an alert.

note.description: Optional note to store with the acknowledgement.

tools.name: rr_trigger_sync
tools.description: Trigger an inventory sync for a connected Shopify or Amazon store. Skipped if a sync ran in the last 5 minutes for this connector type. Returns {status: 'queued'|'skipped', sync_event_id, requested_store_id, blocking_sync_event_id, message}. Pass sync_event_id to rr_get_sync_status to follow the request; sync_run_id is not known at queue time and is always null here. skipped: 'fba_inventory_not_applicable' is permanent for that store (Amazon gives it no FBA inventory access); do not retry it.

store_id.description: Optional store id. If omitted, picks the first connected store of the given platform.

tools.name: rr_set_agent_context
tools.description: Save a small JSON object under a namespace and key, for an agent to read back later. Never store secrets or personal data in it. The namespace must have been granted to this API key.

namespace.description: A context namespace this key has been granted, for example supplier_rules.

key.description: The entry's key within the namespace, up to 200 characters.

value.description: The JSON object to save, up to 16 KiB.

scope_ref.description: Optional label for what the entry is about, up to 200 characters. Not secret.

ttl_seconds.description: Optional lifetime in seconds, up to 90 days.

tools.name: rr_delete_agent_context
tools.description: Delete one saved agent context entry by namespace and key. The namespace must have been granted to this API key.

namespace.description: A context namespace this key has been granted, for example supplier_rules.

key.description: The entry's key within the namespace, up to 200 characters.
